title: Google Sheets and Tally Integration
seoTitle: Google Sheets to Tally: Import Vouchers Without Re-typing
seoDescription: Import vouchers from Google Sheets into TallyPrime and export Tally reports to Sheets automatically. Methods, validation and limits.
summary: A Google Sheets–Tally integration imports vouchers, such as sales, purchases or expenses, from a structured Google Sheet into TallyPrime, and can export Tally reports like outstanding receivables to a sheet on a schedule. It is a practical first step for teams that already collect data in spreadsheets.

dataPoints.label: Sheets side
dataPoints.value: Google Sheets API with a service account and a fixed column layout

dataPoints.label: Tally side
dataPoints.value: TallyPrime XML interface via a connector on the Tally machine

dataPoints.label: Good for
dataPoints.value: Expense claims, branch sales summaries, bulk journal entries, scheduled report exports

dataPoints.label: Validation needed
dataPoints.value: Ledger names, GST rates, dates and duplicate checks before posting

body:
## How it works

1. Staff fill a sheet with a fixed layout and a status column.
2. The integration validates each row: ledger exists, GST rate valid, not already posted.
3. Valid rows post to Tally; the status column shows "posted" or the error.
4. Reports can flow the other way on a schedule, for example outstanding receivables every morning.

## When to move beyond sheets

If the sheet becomes the main system with many users and rules, a small internal app is usually more reliable. See [replacing Excel with custom software](/blog/replacing-excel-with-custom-software-seven-signs-you-have-outgrown-spreadsheets).

faqs.q: Is this safe for accounts data?
faqs.a: Yes, with validation, a posted-status column to prevent duplicates, and limited access to the sheet.

faqs.q: Can it work with Excel files instead?
faqs.a: Yes, files can be uploaded or read from a shared folder, though Google Sheets makes scheduled automation simpler.
